office_does: Yakima County's three commissioners adopt the county budget, pass ordinances, set land-use and permitting rules, and oversee roads and the county landfill; District 1 is elected by its own voters.
race_blurb: An open seat between two Republicans: retiring Sheriff Bob Udell, who won 65% in the primary and stresses budget restructuring and partnerships, and contractor Kristoffer Strutner, who would cut regulation and staff and end the county's well-metering program. Coverage of Strutner centers on the Caton Landfill he operated.

candidates.summary: Two-term Yakima County Sheriff with 36 years in the sheriff's office, running on budget restructuring, partnerships and fiscal responsibility.
highlights: 36 years in the sheriff's office, sheriff since his 2018 election [S1][S2]
Says taxes are a last resort; would restructure county operations and seek revenue through growth [S4]
Priorities: public safety, agriculture, water rights and the budget [S3]

experience.basis: 36 years in county law enforcement, eight as the elected sheriff managing one of the county's largest departments.

taxes.basis: Calls taxes 'a last resort' and would rely on growth for new revenue.

spending.basis: Backs the county's hiring freezes and long-term restructuring, and stresses fiscal responsibility, while supporting public money for an animal shelter.

candidates.summary: Heavy civil construction manager and former Caton Landfill operator promising sweeping cuts to county regulation, permitting and staff.
highlights: Would end the county's well-metering Water Resource System and sell its water rights [S1][S4]
Would cut permitting to state minimums, with 30-minute approvals for stamped plans [S2][S3]
Would reduce county staff as regulation is cut [S4]
Operated the Caton Landfill, which lost its permit; disputes misdemeanor tire-dumping charges [S3]

experience.basis: First-time candidate running on 'experience outside the political system' against a 36-year county official.

housing.basis: Would strip permitting to state minimums, speed approvals, allow rural clustering and end water metering to cut the cost to build.

spending.basis: Would reduce county staff, cut infrastructure costs through contracting changes and liquidate water-rights assets into the general fund.
